newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A broad front of dollar hunters chased the rand to its weakest level in five weeks on Thursday before the Reserve Bank stepped in to defend the local currency which helped it retrace some lost ground.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was at 4.4580/4610 against the dollar from 4.4365/4395 overnight after trading in a 4.4330 to 4.4735 bid range on the day.
The rand was under pressure from the start, dealers said as Far East, London-based and local demand for dollars catapulted the unit four cents weaker from its overnight close.
Dealers said the reasons for the demand stemmed from technically driven short-covering as well as the robust dollar's ascent to fresh highs against the yen and Deutschmark.
The demand for dollars appeared to be most aggressive out of London, one trader said, with local importers also joining the fray.
The currency touched its day's weakest level by around 0650 GMT, 20 minutes after the official opening, before dealers said the Reserve Bank stepped in to calm the market.
"There was a bit of panic buying and then the Reserve Bank put offers in at around 4.4650 and that calmed everybody down," a trader said.
Dealers said that after the central bank's assistance, the market went steadily long dollars, which helped the rand recover to its 1400 GMT level.
The feeling by the end of the day was that the rand had been overdone on the topside and that in the short-term, it looked toppish at around the 4.47 level.
However, the local currency's direction over the next few weeks would be determined by the dollar's movements.

One trader said that despite the U.S. unit's retreat from recent highs against the Deutschmark earlier on Thursday, it could still target the 1.73 level early next week. Dollar/mark was trading at 1.7155 in early New York trade on Thursday.
If that happened, he said the rand could target the 4.49 level.
On Friday, however, position-squaring ahead of the weekend was expected to confine the rand to a 4.45 to 4.4650 range.
The dollar's retreat resulted in the rand giving up some of its recent gainst against the crosses.

It was last quoted at 28.2432/2847 yen after earlier touching a fresh 14-month high of 28.6690, and at 0.3849/3852 marks after touching 0.3893 marks earlier -- also its highest level since February 16 last year.
Direction on the bond market on the day was initially dictated by the rand's movements, which pushed yields about eight basis points up from their overnight levels.

But jobber-short-covering and institutional nibbling at the higher levels brought the R150 back to the middle of its range by 1400 GMT when it was quoted at a 15.22 percent yield from 15.18 percent overnight.
Dealers said the rand's weakness at the start triggered jobber selling which pushed the R150 to 15.26 percent by 0825 GMT, where it held until the release of February producer inflation data.

The producer price index beat market expectations of a 0.7 percent rise when it rose 0.4 percent month-on-month. Dealers said the data triggered jobber short-covering which helped the market retrace to 15.195 percent.
It spent the rest of the afternoon edging higher, keeping half-any eye on continuing weakness on the U.S. Treasury bond market.
Dealers said that while there were some concerns about the rise in the 30-year Treasury bond yield to 7.13 percent from 7.10 percent overnight, they were generally shrugged off.
On Friday the market was expected to hold a 15.20 to 15.26 percent range.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates edged lower to between 16.60 and 16.65 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate held its recent 15.95 to 16.15 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage stood at 8.161 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.899 billion rand on Tuesday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 126.18 million rand's worth of South African bond on Wednesday after buying 156.90 million rand's worth on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 5.25 billion rand from 3.25 billion rand previously.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
